default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-708.title: Dollar-led catch-up
E-708.hypothesis: WIN and the dollar are inversely linked intraday; when the dollar moves sharply and the index has not yet responded, slower index participants reprice and WIN catches up.

E-709.title: Day-open retest hold
E-709.hypothesis: After moving well away from the session open, a return to the open that closes back on the trend side shows the open acting as support/resistance for the day's inventory.

E-710.title: Volatility squeeze release
E-710.hypothesis: Realised volatility far below its 20-session norm means stored-up orders; the first break of the recent range after the squeeze starts a directional expansion.

E-711.title: Afternoon-window range break
E-711.hypothesis: The range built in a late-morning or midday window holds resting orders at its edges; a close outside it later in the session triggers stops and follow-through.

E-712.title: Rolling volume-weighted mean fade
E-712.hypothesis: Price stretched far from the volume-weighted mean of the last hour has been pushed by few participants and tends to revert toward where most volume traded.

E-713.title: Range thrust from the opposite side
E-713.hypothesis: A fast move from the lower half of the recent range to its top (or reverse) within ten minutes shows aggressive one-sided flow that continues.

E-714.title: ATR stretch from EMA fade
E-714.hypothesis: A close several average ranges away from a short EMA is an extension that liquidity takers cannot sustain; fade it back.

E-715.title: Prior-close cross after a stay
E-715.hypothesis: The previous settlement-like close is a reference that market participants anchor to; a first close across it after a stay on one side signals the day's sentiment flipping.

E-716.title: Autocorrelation-regime bar
E-716.hypothesis: When the last hour's bar-to-bar returns are positively autocorrelated a big bar continues; when negatively autocorrelated it reverts. Trade the big bar according to the regime.

E-717.title: Donchian midline cross
E-717.hypothesis: The midpoint of the recent high-low channel separates buyer and seller control; a close crossing it marks a shift in control that persists.
